blocks.text: **The task.** An array contains N distinct numbers taken from the range 0 to N. Exactly one is missing — find it.
Put every value at its matching index, then scan for the index that does not match.
The guard `target < nums.length` matters. The range is 0 to N **inclusive**, so the value N is legal but has no index N to sit at — it stays wherever it lands and the mismatch scan finds the gap.
The final `return nums.length` covers the case where nothing is out of place, meaning N itself is what is missing.
Shorter and arguably better here. The numbers 0 to N sum to a known value, so the missing one is the shortfall:
O(N) time, O(1) space, no mutation. The one caveat is overflow for very large N in fixed-width integer languages — JavaScript is safe well past any realistic array size.
Avoids overflow entirely. XOR every index and every value together; identical pairs cancel and the missing number survives alone:

The sum formula is clearest. XOR is the safest under overflow. Cyclic sort is the one that generalises — when a problem asks for *all* missing numbers, or mixes missing with duplicated, the sum trick collapses and cyclic sort keeps working.
